paper_metadata.title: Generative Knowledge Graph Construction: A Review
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2022)
paper_metadata.abstract: This review defines generative knowledge graph construction as sequence-to-sequence methods for building knowledge graphs. It summarizes recent generative KGC progress, compares paradigm advantages and weaknesses by generation target, provides theoretical and empirical analyses, and proposes future research directions.

problem_addressed: A survey problem: generative KGC methods had become distributed across entity recognition, relation extraction, event extraction, entity linking, and KG completion, without a systematic review or common comparison. The paper organizes and analyzes these methods, which use Seq2Seq generation to extract or generate KG-relevant structures from text and thereby avoid the task-specific pipeline limitations of error propagation and poor cross-task adaptability.

methodology.description: The paper surveys generative KGC as conditional sequence generation: unstructured text x is mapped to a linearized structural target y, then inverse-linearized or decoded into entities, relations/triples, event structures, links, or KG-completion outputs. It proposes five generation-target paradigms in execution terms: (1) copy-based sequences copy entity tokens while generating relation tokens from a restricted vocabulary; (2) structure-linearized sequences serialize a target graph/event/triple structure, often with schema-constrained decoding; (3) label-augmented sequences reproduce input text with bracketed natural-language labels; (4) indice-based sequences generate begin/end and label indices via pointer-style decoding; and (5) blank-based sequences fill role placeholders in event templates. The review compares semantic utilization, decoding search space, application scope, and template cost; theoretically analyzes output-space/semantic trade-offs and decoding; and aggregates reported NYT and ACE-2005 results from prior work. Contributions explicitly stated by the authors are a detailed taxonomy, theoretical and empirical analysis, and future directions.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Schema use is central to several reviewed generative approaches. Targets may be restricted to a predefined schema; structural/event schemas constrain decoding and validate semantic/structural legitimacy. The review describes prefix-tree decoding based on predefined schemas and label-semantic or template-based representations. It does not propose a new ontology or schema itself.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured natural-language text, including sentences and documents; certain reviewed methods additionally take a schema, task specification, or event template as input.
input_output.input_granularity: Sentence-level examples are used for NER, relation extraction, entity linking, and triple generation; the review also covers document-level relation and event extraction.
input_output.output_representation: Linearized structure sequences that can be inverse-linearized into typed entities, entity links, relation triples, event triggers/arguments, or KG-completion answers. Formats include copied token spans plus relation tokens, serialized triples/structures, label-augmented text, input-token indices, and filled natural-language templates.

value: NYT relation extraction: DEEPSTRUCT reports F1 93.9; UIE 93.5; CGT P/R/F 94.7/84.2/89.1; REBEL 91.5/92.0/91.8; TANL F1 90.8. The reported discriminative reference values are CasRel 89.6 F1, TPLinker 92.0, and OneRel 92.8.
NYT non-autoregressive methods: SPN reports P/R/F 93.3/91.7/92.5; Seq2UMTree reports 79.1/75.1/77.1.

ACE-2005 event extraction: DEEPSTRUCT reports trigger identification/classification F1 73.5/69.8 and argument identification/classification F1 59.4/56.2. UIE reports trigger classification 73.4 and argument classification 54.8; TEXT2EVENT 71.9 and 53.8 respectively. PAIE, evaluated only for argument extraction with golden triggers, reports argument identification/classification 75.7/72.7.

Authors' synthesis: structure- and label-based approaches achieve similar extraction performance to the cited discriminative methods on NYT; generative methods are comparable on ACE-2005 event extraction. These are cross-paper tabulations, not controlled head-to-head experiments run by this survey.

[Review-level inference] The reported values support treating the paper as a comparative synthesis, not as evidence that any one method is universally superior, because tasks, method groups, and (for PAIE) evaluation conditions differ.

value: Provides a task-by-generation-target taxonomy that covers five Seq2Seq paradigms across NER, relation extraction, event extraction, entity linking, and KG completion.
Links the taxonomy to an explicit comparative framework: semantic utilization, search space, application scope, and template cost.
Combines conceptual/theoretical analysis of output-space and decoding trade-offs with tabulated empirical results on NYT and ACE-2005.

Identifies schema-guided decoding, non-autoregressive generation, unified architectures, and decoding efficiency as concrete design concerns rather than presenting generation as categorically superior.

[Review-level inference] Its tables and figures make it useful as a methodological map for selecting a generation representation, but the paper's evidence remains a secondary synthesis of prior studies.

value: The review's scope is limited to generative KGC, so it does not comprehensively evaluate non-generative extraction, fusion, validation, or updating pipelines.
The empirical analysis is limited to two benchmark settings and imports results from existing papers rather than running a unified controlled evaluation.
The five paradigm categories can overlap in practice: schema constraints can make a structure-based method's decoding space resemble a copy-based method's, complicating strict category boundaries.
Autoregressive decoding incurs sequential inference cost and can suffer exposure bias/overfitting; some index-based formats also sacrifice label/text semantics for a smaller output space.

[Review-level inference] The cross-paper comparisons should be interpreted as descriptive because the survey does not establish uniform implementations, splits, preprocessing, or evaluation protocols across every result it tabulates.

value: How to balance a constrained output/search space, which can ease optimization, against rich use of label and text semantics.
How to ensure output quality, including reliable and semantically/structurally legitimate generated structures.
How to obtain efficient inference without autoregressive sequential decoding, exposure bias, or propagation of prediction deviations.
How to build universal models that transfer across KGC tasks, domains, datasets, and potentially modalities while preserving task-specific performance.
How to integrate symbolic structure and generative NLP more effectively.

[Review-level inference] Broad Text-to-KG stages such as coreference resolution, entity deduplication/fusion, graph validation/correction, and graph updating receive no sustained treatment in this generative-extraction-focused survey; their integration with the five paradigms remains unresolved within this paper's coverage.
